papers.what_it_is: A paper that defines quantum natural gradient descent for variational circuits as steepest descent in the Fubini-Study metric (real part of the quantum geometric tensor), gives a circuit method for its block-diagonal approximation, and compares it with gradient descent, Adam and gradient-free optimizers in simulation.

papers.title_in_file: Fourier Fingerprints of Ansatzes in Quantum Machine Learning
papers.what_it_is: A numerical study arguing that efficiently-trainable quantum Fourier models must have correlated Fourier coefficients, defining a Fourier coefficient correlation (FCC) metric and 'Fourier fingerprint' per ansatz, and testing whether the FCC predicts ansatz performance on random Fourier series and a high-energy-physics jet dataset in simulation.

existing.note: Section 2.1 gives the reasoning: the number of Fourier terms grows exponentially while efficient training needs polynomially many parameters (training time is linear in the parameter count), so asymptotically there is no injective map from parameters to coefficients and coefficients must share parameters.
existing.value: The authors argue that typical encodings give quantum Fourier models with O(exp(n)) Fourier basis functions while efficient trainability needs O(poly(n)) parameters, since training time is linear in the parameter count; so in the asymptotic limit there is no injective map between Fourier coefficients and parameters, the coefficients must depend on shared parameters, and this implies correlations between Fourier modes that depend on the circuit structure.
quotes: Typical schemes to encode classical data in variational quantum machine learning (QML) lead to quantum Fourier models with O(exp(n)) Fourier basis functions in the number of qubits.
Despite this, in order for the model to be efficiently trainable, the number of parameters must scale as O(poly(n)).
This imbalance implies the existence of correlations between the Fourier modes, which depend on the structure of the circuit.
since the time complexity of training is linear in |θ|.
it is immediately apparent that in the asymptotic limit there is no injective map between the set of Fourier coefficients cω and θ.
Therefore, the coefficients cω(θ) must depend on a shared set of ansatz parameters, which implies the existence of correlations between the coefficients of different terms in the Fourier series.
existing.certainty_reason: An informal counting argument; the paper's appendix proposition is stated without a full proof, and the authors note the guarantee is only asymptotic for feature maps with exponentially many unique frequencies.
existing.reader_inference: A non-injective map shows coefficients cannot all be set independently; that this appears as nonzero Pearson correlation over random parameters is shown numerically, not proved.

quotes: we note that correlations between the Fourier coefficients of efficientlytrainable QFMs are only asymptotically guaranteed for feature maps that produce exponentially many unique frequencies.
Finally, in this work, we studied only one instance of a real-world dataset.
existing.certainty_reason: The paper's own stated limits, Section 4.

existing.note: Section 3.1 shows the 1D relation is almost linear, but in 2D Circuit 15 is an outlier (it lacks imaginary coefficients under the RX feature map), and the target series' frequencies were set equal to the model's own frequencies. The conclusion's 'consistently' is stronger than the 2D figure.
existing.value: The authors report, in simulations with 100 runs per ansatz, that for learning random Fourier series whose frequencies were set to match the models' own frequencies, the FCC correlates almost linearly with the MSE in 1D and that models with lower average FCC perform better in 1D and 2D, except that in 2D Circuit 15 is an outlier; the expressibility metric fails to predict the order of the MSE.
quotes: The frequencies of the dataset Ωˆ are explicitly set to the same frequencies as those generated by the FM of the QFM models Ω.
Specifically, we use 10 different model initialization and 10 different dataset seeds, yielding a total of 100 runs per ansatz.
we observe that, overall, the FCC correlates almost linearly with the MSE, with the lowest and highest values of the FCC being 4.57 × 10−3 (Circuit 15 ) and 0.323 (Circuit 18 ), respectively.
Here, one can see that Circuit 15 is now an outlier in the otherwise almost linear relationship between MSE and FCC.
In Sec. 3.1, we showed how, for the task of learning random Fourier series, models with lower average FCC consistently perform better for both 1D and 2D inputs.
The expressibility, in contrast, does not allow for a conclusive statement and fails to correctly predict the order of the final MSE for every ansatz.

Practically, this implies that QFMs cannot independently control each frequency.
